items.sentence: The fraction of blood the left ventricle ejects each beat. Sources differ on the lower limit of normal: British Society of Echocardiography reporting categories treat 55% or more as normal (50 to 54% is borderline low), while the BHF and NHS England describe 50% or more as normal. In heart failure classification, a reduced ejection fraction is usually taken as 40% or less.
items.note: Second pass: BSE 2020 gives normal as 55% or more (first pass used the trust sheet's '>55%'); NHS England glossary 50% or higher; HFrEF 40% or less from NICE TA773 (BHF booklet says less than 40%).

items.sentence: Ejection fraction well below normal -> Significantly reduced pumping; heart-failure treatment is considered
items.note: Qualitative rewrite of 'Ejection fraction 30% ... start heart-failure treatment'; no number kept.
